:::{#exm-quadratic-model}
#### The quadratic approximation at $x = 2.5$

For $f(x) = \tfrac{1}{3} x^3 - 4x$ at $x = 2.5$ (@exm-newton-method),

$$
\begin{aligned}
g &= 2.5^2 - 4 \\
&= 2.25
\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}
H &= [2 \cdot 2.5] \\
&= [5],
\end{aligned}
$$

so
$\quadmodelf{\step} = f(2.5) + 2.25\,\step + 2.5\,\step^2$.
For $f(\vx) = \tfrac{1}{2} (x_1^2 + 3 x_2^2)$, whose Hessian is $\sbmat{ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 }$ at every point,
the [quadratic approximation](#def-quadratic-model) at any $\vx$ equals $f(\vx + \stepvec)$ exactly (@exm-taylor-mv with $\matr{S} = \sbmat{ 1/2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3/2 }$). <!-- check-term-links: allow: equality of two numbers, not the matrix or complex-number equality that the term names -->

<!-- no-figure: the approximation at x = 2.5 is graphed with its Newton step in the figure after exm-newton-model -->

:::
